neighbours.label: the end of a clause that states an inference about what an observation means (could only have been ..., any other explanation ...)
fire: The footprints were enormous, and they could only have been left by a bear.
Such precise carvings could only have been made with metal tools.
The pattern in the data has no other explanation than a calibration error.
The fossils sat above the ash layer, so they must be younger than the eruption.
Since the door was locked from inside, the thief could only have used the window.
The signal repeated every hour, which can only mean it was man-made.
The ink had not faded at all, so the letter must have been written recently.
Is there any other explanation for the missing funds than theft?
quiet: The footprints were enormous, and we followed them up the hill.
Such precise carvings were displayed in the museum's main hall.
The pattern in the data was shown in the second figure.
The fossils sat above the ash layer, and we photographed them.
Since the door was locked from inside, we waited in the garden.
The signal repeated every hour, and the station logged each one.
The ink had not faded at all, and the paper was still white.
Is there any coffee left in the pot from this morning?

notes: card: peaks on ',' '.' 'but' 'explanation' in arguments about what something must be; the - pole fires on 'could only', 'would not be expected'. probe: 'could only have been produced by a faulty sensor.' 0.81 at '.', 'any other explanation than' 0.32; narrative 0.01.
